fix(material/chips): chip set overwriting disabled state (#29795)

The chip set has been set up in a way where it syncs its state to the chips, instead of the other way around which we follow in other components. This means that if its `disabled` state changes later, it can ovewrite the state that the user explicitly set on the chip.

These changes make the logic a bit more robust by writing to a different field.

Fixes #29783.
decision: Full original four-path patch reviewed: modern chip-set sync moves list disabled writes off the individual disabled input, chip getter combines both flags, listbox forms regression reproduces loss on NgModel initialization, and API guard reflects getter/setter separation. Untouched Material16 legacy chip/list already implement this separate-field contract, including original toggle regression; this is a real behavioral analogue, not a docs-only or ancestry exclusion. The old main already-adapted entry cited field names and omitted the test/API paths, with no executed forms regression. Preserve that historical conclusion but reopen release admission until the newly added exact forms initialization/aria regression and packed template/reactive disable-enable case execute against actual artifact. No product repair appears needed; candidate chip/list implementation remains unchanged. Stable current forms peers must run the actual legacy value accessor. New packed case is distinct and mandatory in both actual line rosters; false/omitted/forged reports fail admission controls. Native/AOT/packed execution is pending; no sensitive or complete G11 pass.
